I spent far too much time thinking about this.

I gave the Champion tier to Legacy. He's just too iconic, and traditionally powerful. I figured that Mainstay beat Tachyon to show how cool he was, went down to unconventional Tempest tactics, and then Legacy beat Tempest. 

Tech Tier to Writhe, narrowly. I figure he could handle Bunker and Benchmark, opening the door to a really cool final battle against Parse.

Mystic Tier to the Argent Adept, also narrowly. Idealist can stomp Harpy, and Medico seems tailor-made to beat Nightmist through outlasting and overwhelming her, but then Medico throws the fight against the Idealist because he can't bear to really go all-in. Meanwhile, the Visionary stomps over the Scholar because the Scholar isn't going all in, and the Adept beats the Visionary because we know the Adept fought and defeated the Visionary here. 

Martial Tier: Mr. Fixer is in his element, and wins. He beats Wraith in order to have a cool story rematch against Expatriette. Setback gets past KNYFE and Guise through luck, and then founders against style.

Conquerer Tier: Progeny, duh. I considered Zhu Long, just because we know he is scary-powerful, but while he probaby wipes the floor with Kaargra and Infinitor, I don't see him having much of an edge on the big silver lug.

Cunning Tier: It's got to be Baron Blade. Unless there was a heck of an upset, I can't see him losing out. I imagine a final battle against Glamour that involved him seeing through her tricks.

Eldritch Tier: Definitely Lifeline. He's a token evil person fighting other evil people to advance; he needs to reach a point where he fights a hero.

Bruiser Tier: After a lot of consideration, Fright Train. I think he could take Plague Rat and Sergeant Steel, and while I'm betting on Spite against Bugbear (just because Bugbear is best at tearing apart weaker foes) I think Spite couldn't get much purchase against the Train.

Finale: Legacy somehow beats Progeny, using the skills and understanding that he's learned since their last fight. Baron Blade crushes Writhe. Lifeline deliberately throws his match against the Argent Adept. Fright Train flattens Mister Fixer by being just generally immune to martial arts. This leaves two Hero Vs Villain fights.

The big twist - Baron Blade beats Legacy! Maniacal laughter going into the finale. And Argent Adept out-magics Fright Train, for a Magic VS Science grand finale in which the human spirit pretty much has to triumph, so the Argent Adept is the big winner. 

 

*EDIT* Ah, crap, my bracket is almost certainly wrong. I think Yoshi is right - if Blade beat Legacy, it would be something that Christopher and Adam would have mentioned in the Blade episode.

Well, I already sent my form in, but my revised guess is Progeny beats Legacy, Blade beats Progeny.

Urgh, the whole "Spite, Agent of Gloom" thing is really throwing me off.  He's extremely strong and dangerous, but the Gloomweaver episode has him come to life and immediately get beaten down by the heroes.  I can't reconcile that with the Cosmic Contest timeline at all, especially given that this is Skinwalker Gloomweaver, as well, in Spite's body.  I can only infer that C&A didn't put too much thought into this part, and Spite gets beaten and sent back to his grave quickly.

Edit: Well, I think I'm done, but I ended up with a very different bracket from what anyone else is describing.  Basically I went up and down the tree asking myself what confrontation would be the most interesting at any given point.  Much less about fighting and more about talking.  I gave more time to characters introduced later in the story who would have most benefitted from exposition and self-awareness opportunities, and usually chose winners based on what would be the most dramatic or powerful storytelling.  For instance, I'll leave you all with a bit of fan-fiction:

-------------------

Parse crept across the arena, arrow in hand.  Her eyes darted from obstacle to obstacle, her every sense alert to the slightest hint of motion.  "I know you well, robot.  I've studied your code.  Every algorithm, every subroutine.  I can anticipate every move you make, every move you are capable of making.  This can only end one way."

"Well-reasoned, Kim Howell," the mechanical voice echoed from a point not far away.  Parse was instantly in motion.  "Your calculations are flawless, as always.  But any calculation will fail when based on false assumptions."

Parse was only half-listening; the voice emanated from just beyond the next pile of crates.  She crept along quietly as the voice continued.  "You know my computer programming, yes, the code of Omnitron.  But I am not Omnitron anymore.  I am Omnitron-U.  The "U" comes from Unity.  My friend.  She is a part of me now.  And that part is human."

The arrow flew from Parse's hand and struck true with a satisfying crunch of machinery.  But what was it she'd hit?  She picked it up.  Part of a... toy dinosaur?  Why would a robot.... Belatedly, she realized what Omnitron-U had been saying.  Of course, no computer would have thought of such a diversion, given the limited resources in the arena.  He stood behind her now, weapons bristling.  She raised her hands in surrender.

"Our friends are always a part of us, Kim Howell."  The voice, slightly garbled now, still came from the toy.  Omnitron-U reached around, took a component out of it, and inserted it under his "chin."  "It is a lesson I am still learning."

"I never had any friends," Parse murmured, half to herself, still not really thinking of the robot as a person.

"Perhaps it is time for that to change, Kim.  But for now, it is time for you to return home."
